title.narrative: Bangladesh Strengthening PFM Program to Enable Service Delivery

description.narrative: The Program Development Objective (PDO) is to improve fiscal forecasting, budget preparation and execution, financial reporting and transparency to enable better resource availability for service delivery in selected Ministries, Departments, and Agencies.

The development objective of the Strengthening Public Financial Management (PFM) Program to Enable Service Delivery - Program-for-Results (PforR) Project for Bangladesh is to improve fiscal forecasting, budget preparation, and execution, financial reporting and transparency to enable better resource availability for service delivery in selected Ministries, Departments, and Agencies. This document describes the context, rationale, and objectives of the World Bank's support to a new government program for strengthening PFM in Bangladesh. This PFM action plan provides the implementation road map for priority actions. The government has requested the International Development Association (IDA) PforR operation to support the Ministry of Finance (MoF) in implementing selected components of the PFM action plan. The document also summarizes the relevant assessments, including the technical aspects such as the best-fit, program results framework, cost-benefit, and fiduciary and social and environmental safeguard risks.

title.narrative: SOE and autonomous bodiesâ€™ debt and contingent liabilities statement prepared and submitted to appropriate authority

baseline.value: - SOE debt and contingent liabilities are not effectively controlled- Partial data of SOEs profitability published in the annual Economic Survey of Bangladesh- Fiscal risks assessments have not been conducted

target.value: - Policy and procedures to regulate SOEsâ€™ debt and contingent liabilities (including an upgraded framework for reporting by SOEs to the Finance Division) have been drafted and issued by MoF.- 100 SOEs and autonomous bodies have published their audited financialtatements (covering the relevant Fiscal Year for which the DLR is being assessed).- SOE debt and contingent liabilities statement (covering the relevant Fiscal Year for which the DLR is being assessed) has been prepared by MoF for all SOEs and submitted to appropriate authority.

actual.value: FD conducted several rounds of focused trainings for SOEs on disclosure of Debt and Contingent Liabilities (DCL) and pre-requisite information for SOE database. The first-cut DCL statements, based on FY22 data for 50 SOEs, have been completed and disbursement processed preparation of rest 50 SOEs are underway.

title.narrative: Improved budget alignment with development strategy through better performance of BMCs
Budget holders in selected MDAs effectively and transparently use financial information
Reduced number of days for DDOs to receive budget in selected MDAs
Timely and reliable payments of salaries and vendor invoices with a strengthened TSA and automated payment system

baseline.value: EFT used for officersâ€™ salaries only. No online bills submission. Stock take of special accounts & EBFs will be done.

target.value: - 50% EFT- 40% DDOs submitting online bills- Number of new (outside TSA) special accounts opened annually reduced by 50%

actual.value: (i) Using the newly developed online system, bank account information has been entered for 55,675 government offices (out of 90,000 government offices), totaling 137,546 bank accounts; and (iii) the bills for 98 percent pay and allowances, 98 percent pension payments and almost 80 percent Social Safety Net payments are submitted online and made through Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT).

title.narrative: Action taken on internal and external audit reports in Selected MDAs and post-procurement reviews in the Finance Division

baseline.value: Internal audit units are not effective. Internal audit activities consist primarily of ex-post reviews focused on financial compliance.

target.value: - The Model Internal Audit Charter and the Risk-based Internal Audit Manual have been issued by the Finance Division. - A system for annual procurement planning and post-review has been established by the Finance Division and training on the system has been conducted. - Internal audit reports, prepared in accordance with the Model Internal Audit Charter and the Risk-based Internal Audit Manual issued, have been issued to the heads of departments and principal accounting officers of any two departments in any of the Selected MDAs. The relevant Internal Audit Committees (IAC) of Ministries/ Divisions prepares an action plan to resolve at least 25% of:I. Internal audit observations of the report of two selected departmentsand II. Procurement post-review findings of SPFMS program of Finance Division.

actual.value: -The Internal Audit Charter and Manual have been finalized and approved by the Senior Secretary, Finance. -Several view exchange meetings were conducted in the individual department with the officials of the selected high spending Ministries i.e., PWD, RHD, LGED, DGHS, and DPE. These covered the existing system of internal audit, the present status of internal audit in the departments, future action plans for the internal audit system, etc. Sr. Consultants had submitted five separate study reports to the PIT. -training on Risk-based Internal Audit for Government officials was conducted by the scheme on Internal Audit and Audit Follow- up and the Institute of Internal Auditors Bangladesh (IIAB). This training was designed especially for the selected five high-spending MDAs (Ministries/ Departments/ Agencies) and Finance Division. MDAs are LGED, PWD, RHD, DGHS, DPE, and FD. - Senior Consultant (Procurement) has conducted the post procurement review of all schemes under the SPFMS.

baseline.value: PFM reform implementation, monitoring, and course-correction are not adequately coordinated, and a comprehensive change management approach needs to be implemented

target.value: - Two PFM Action Plan progress reports (prepared on a semi-annual basis) have been submitted by the PECT to the Steering Committee. - Two PFM Action Plan stakeholder retreats conducted to review the respective semi-annual PFM Action Plan progress reports prepare under DLR 10.1.- The PFM Learning Hub has produced at least 3 research papers on PFM reform lessons and published the said reports through its website.- 6 field inspections to government service delivery centers to identify PFM-related issues have been carried out.- The PECT has prepared a report evaluating the performance of coaches, facilitators and/or implementation support consultants engaged to support the implementation of the PFM Action Plan.- 100 civil servants (with data disaggregated by gender) have completd specialized PFM-related courses/certifications.

title.narrative: Improved performance, reporting, and public disclosure of the SOEs/ABs

baseline.value: SOEs are not classified as commercial and non-commercial.There is some performance monitoring of SOEs, but not systematic and independent.Grants to SOEs are not divided into different categories.Partial data of SOEs profitability published in the annual Economic Survey of Bangladesh.

target.value: - SOE performance evaluation guidelines have been developed by the Finance Division, with clear scoring criteria.- A policy and procedures manual for property, plant, equipment and other assets that enables to ensure the quality of management and accounting procedure has been drafted and issued by the Finance Division.- At least 10 SOEs have undergone an independent performance evaluation, in accordance with the SOE performance evaluation guidelines developed. - Turnaround strategies have been developed for the identified underperforming SOEs.

actual.value: SOE performance evaluation guidelines have been developed by the Finance Division, with clear scoring criteria. Several SOEs have undergone an independent performance evaluation, in accordance with the SOE performance evaluation guidelines developed. Performance evaluation of ten SOEs have also been completed in accordance with the SOE performance evaluation guidelines. A comprehensive policy and procedures manual for property, plant, equipment (PPE), and other assets is being prepared, with efforts to standardize measurement and management across key sectors. An inception workshop was successfully held on February 2, 2024, and visits to 17 SOEs (7 in Dhaka, 6 in Chittagong, and 4 in Sylhet) have been completed. These visits focused on gathering data regarding depreciation, fixed assets management systems, and accounting practices.

title.narrative: Improved Pension Service (disaggregated by gender) through facilitation of payments through EFT no later than the pension payment cycle following retirement

baseline.value: - Long process often results in a significant delay after retirement to prepare a Pension Payment Order- All pension and GP fund records are manual and prone to human errors

target.value: - The GP Fund Module and the Pension Service Module of iBAS++ have been implemented and are operational.- A centralized pension roll with EFT payment capability has been established and is operational.- A government-wide annual GPF and Pension Service report has been produced.- The number of cases of delayed pension payments is reduced by 50%. - 90% of new pensioners are paid through EFT no later than the pension payment cycle following their retirement.

actual.value: The backlog of delayed pension cases has been reduced by 89 percent (out of 744 cases in 2020). The pension Call Center and grievance handling mechanism are fully functional and receive high regards by the pensioners.
